content: Marsh Labrador Tea, also known as Northern Labrador Tea or Wild Rosemary, is a flowering plant scientifically classified as Rhododendron tomentosum (formerly Ledum palustre). It belongs to the subsection Ledum within the large genus Rhododendron in the family Ericaceae. This plant is a low-growing shrub that typically reaches a height of 50 cm, although in rare cases, it can grow up to 120 cm tall. Its leaves are evergreen, measuring between 12-50 mm in length and 2-12 mm in width. The flowers of Marsh Labrador Tea are small and feature a five-lobed white corolla. These flowers are grouped together in clusters called corymbs, which are 3-5 cm in diameter. The plant emits a strong odor, which serves to attract bees and other pollinating insects. Geographically, this plant is found in northern latitudes across North America, including Greenland, Canada, and Alaska. In Europe, its range extends as far south as Germany, while in Asia, it is found as far south as northern China, Korea, and Japan. It thrives in environments with peaty soils, shrubby areas, moss, and lichen tundra. Historically, Marsh Labrador Tea has been used in traditional herbal medicine, as detailed under the broader topic of Labrador Tea. During the Middle Ages, it was also utilized as a gruit, an ingredient in brewing beer. However, all parts of this plant contain toxic terpenes, which can affect the central nervous system. These compounds are known to induce aggressive behavior. Additionally, the mere smell of the plant can cause headaches in some individuals.
